> I've retested this PR (rebased on top of `master` [2d86b69](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/2d86b69bf1e82f703cc0543d4309a9c8a4198585)), and this is what I get with the linked project when using Mobile:

The problem you have seems to be related to fp16, and I don't have a system that supports that very well, but I tried to make some adjustments to see if it works for you now.
This patch should fix the fp16 issues: [half_clearcoat.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23723604/half_clearcoat.patch)

@BlueCube3310 Thank you for the correction.
If I didn't make any mistake, this should now work fine with fp16.

Removed the redundant code from half_inc.glsl (saturateHvec2(x), saturateHvec3(x), and saturateHvec4(x)). I realized that using clamp(x, 0.0, 1.0) in f0_Clear_Coat_To_Surface() was necessary, as its absence caused artifacts when dealing with low roughness and clearcoat_roughness values.

> Looks very good! I tested locally and it works as expected. The code seems to be correct as well, I compared it with the Filament document and it looks like this matches its implementation correctly.

There are two things worth mentioning regarding Google Filament’s implementation:

- Filament applies specular antialiasing to the clearcoat. [Link](https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_shading_lit.fs#L176-L179)
- Filament uses a hack with roughness and clearcoat roughness to ensure the base layer and the clearcoat layer share the same roughness level. [Link](https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_shading_lit.fs#L208-L214)

I'm not entirely sure about adding these two features. Godot doesn't originally apply specular antialiasing to the clearcoat, and regarding the roughness trick, I'm unsure of its physical basis. Furthermore, Godot limits clearcoat roughness, so it can never become fully diffuse.

just noticed that you are multiplying `cc_attenuation` against the backlight in scene.glsl (Compatibility) but not in forward_lights_inc (Forward). Is this a mistake, or is there a reason? I'm asking because I am copying the changes across to area lights.

> just noticed that you are multiplying `cc_attenuation` against the backlight in scene.glsl (Compatibility) but not in forward_lights_inc (Forward). Is this a mistake, or is there a reason? I'm asking because I am copying the changes across to area lights. Yeah, it looks like the `cc_attenuation` multiplication was indeed left in the backlight for the Compatibility render. To be honest, I'm not entirely sure if we should be doing this multiplication in the backlight or not; you can't really see much of a difference at a glance, and it’s only noticeable if there are no shadows covering the back. |Without `cc_attenuation`|With `cc_attenuation`| |-------------------------------|-------------------------------| |||
